date_note: Date of the Town's release giving the recovery update, as dated in the Rio Rancho Observer article; the article says the attack itself was on Oct. 10.
exec: A New Mexico town said many online services were still unavailable after a cyberattack, while its offices stayed open in person.
geo_basis: town named in the source (Bernalillo; town centre approximate)
plain: The Town of Bernalillo said it is making progress restoring its systems after a cyberattack. Many online services were still unavailable, but all town offices were open for in-person business.
summary: The Rio Rancho Observer reports that a Nov. 24 release from Mayor Jack Torres announced progress restoring critical services after a cyberattack on the Town of Bernalillo, which the article says began on Oct. 10. The article says billing access was frozen, many online services remained unavailable and all town offices were open for in-person business. It gives no attack type or attacker.
title: Town of Bernalillo, New Mexico updates residents on recovery from cyberattack, per its release

validation.note: Rio Rancho Observer and Cedar News both relay the same town release; one underlying statement, so single source. The town's own release was not read.

review.note: Compared Nov 24 release, Oct 10 attack, billing, offices open with Rio Rancho Observer; Cedar News is a copy, single_source ok
